title: Grateful Dead Live at Wembley Empire Pool on 1972-04-07
lineage: 2 AUD sources: MR> C> CDR + M?> low-gen reel> CDR (see info file)

ai_review.summary: A legendary Europe‑'72 performance with scorching sets (Truckin’, The Other One, China>Rider) but captured on two horrendous audience tapes that are nearly unlistenable.
ai_review.review: The show is widely praised for its high energy, blistering first‑set work and a monster second set featuring Truckin'>Drums>Too>El Paso>Wharf Rat and an incendiary The Other One.  Unfortunately the only available sources are two audience recordings that reviewers describe as “the worst quality of any Dead recording,” sounding like they were taped from the bottom of a pool, with severe muffling and inconsistency.  For completists the music is worth hearing; for most listeners the audio makes it a painful experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the performance very highly (average ~4.5/5) but uniformly condemn the recording quality (~1/5). Weighted 70% show + 30% recording yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Two audience (AUD) sources; described as horrendous, muffled, inconsistent, sounding like a mic in a pool or on a roof. Frequent drop‑outs, lack of instrument separation, and overall unlistenable.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A marathon first set that builds momentum, followed by a second‑set ‘meat’ sequence (Truckin' → Drums → Too → El Paso → Too → Wharf Rat) praised for its seamless segues and high‑octane improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly lauded for his soaring tone, powerful solos (especially in Truckin' and The Other One), and overall fire throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as ‘bombing’ with a thunderous bass line that drives the extended Too jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Described as “on fire” early in the set, delivering strong vocals and energetic rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brief mention of interplay between Jerry and Keith (keyboard) during The Other One; otherwise not highlighted.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming praised as other‑worldly, especially in the intense meat sequence.
